title: Saturday, November 28
script:
Good morning. It is Saturday, November 28, 2026.

Starting with the weather in Arkadelphia, expect a partly sunny afternoon with a high near sixty-eight degrees and temperatures falling to around sixty-four degrees. South southwest winds will move at around five miles per hour with gusts up to twenty miles per hour, and there is a zero percent chance of rain. Tonight brings mostly cloudy skies with a chance of rain showers after three a.m. The low will be around fifty-four degrees, with temperatures rising to around fifty-eight degrees overnight. South winds will blow at five to fifteen miles per hour with gusts reaching thirty miles per hour, and a thirty percent chance of precipitation. Sunday turns partly sunny with a high near sixty-three degrees, falling to around fifty-two degrees in the afternoon. West winds will reach twenty to twenty-five miles per hour with gusts up to forty miles per hour, and an eleven percent chance of rain. A Wind Advisory is currently in effect. Sunrise will be at six fifty-seven a.m. and sunset at five oh two p.m.

Moving to the top headlines around the world. U.S. Army officials called the controlled detonation of roughly five tons of explosive lead azide in Iowa a success, with initial EPA tests showing no toxic lead contamination, though critics have pointed to a lack of transparency regarding the operation. United Nations climate talks at COP31 collapsed after failing to reach an agreement on language regarding fossil fuels that cause global warming, as several countries and the European Union refused to accept a final proposal without explicit mentions. In Afghanistan, an explosion at a school in the eastern part of the country killed ten students and wounded one hundred and ten, with local officials stating the blast appeared to have originated in a neighboring depot for mining explosives. Meanwhile, next week marks the start of construction on a new aircraft carrier named the USS Doris Miller, honoring the Pearl Harbor hero who carried the wounded to safety and fired a machine gun at Japanese planes.

Let's look at the latest in football. The Kansas City Chiefs are dealing with the aftermath of a thirteen to ten Thanksgiving night loss to the Buffalo Bills in a cold, rainy game where offensive mistakes and special teams blunders cost them a victory. Despite the setback, a Broncos loss keeps the AFC West race alive, and the team now faces a tough December schedule with major playoff implications following a performance where running back Emmett Johnson managed ninety-six total yards on twenty-one touches. Elsewhere in the NFL, the Rams confirmed that Davante Adams will not return from his injury, while guard Steve Avila could potentially return for the Week thirteen game against the Chiefs.

Turning to Kansas men's basketball, No. 12 Kansas pulled away late for a sixty-five to fifty win over Villanova on Friday night. White scored seventeen points and Stokes added fourteen as the Jayhawks survived a Villanova scare to cap a fiery start to the season, with head coach Bill Self praising Tyran Stokes's performance as he works his way back to one hundred percent health.

Checking your fantasy football radar for week twelve, several key players have been ruled out for Sunday, including Brock Purdy with an ankle injury, Justin Herbert with a concussion, Parker Washington with a shoulder issue, and Bhayshul Tuten with an ankle and foot injury. Managers should look to the waiver wire and injury replacement lists for immediate fill-ins, keeping an eye on targets like Brock Bowers and running back start and sit options as the weekend matchups get underway.

Now for the weather in Los Angeles. Today brings mostly cloudy skies with a high near seventy-six degrees and east southeast winds from zero to five miles per hour. The chance of rain is one percent. Tonight stays mostly cloudy with a low around fifty-seven degrees and light winds, with a zero percent chance of rain. Sunday brings mostly sunny skies and a high near seventy-three degrees with southeast winds around five miles per hour and a three percent chance of rain. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise will be at six thirty-eight a.m. and sunset at four forty-three p.m.

In Hollywood and screenwriting news. The five-day Thanksgiving box office stretch is coming in at an estimated over two hundred and twenty million dollars, led by the continued dominance of The Hunger Games prequel Sunrise on the Reaping, which is warming up an eighty-three million dollar plus five-day haul. OpenAI has filed a countersuit against Apple accusing the tech giant of unlawfully pressuring vendors following Apple's earlier lawsuit this summer. Meanwhile, NBC has pulled a controversial ad critical of U.S. military aid to Israel that aired during the Saturday Night Live Thanksgiving special without senior management's knowledge, and Gayle King is taking next week off from CBS Mornings following the death of her son-in-law, Virgil Miller.

In artificial intelligence and tech. SEBI is exploring the development of an India-built AI model specifically for the securities market, alongside plans to train engineers for the initiative. E2E Networks has won a fourteen point sixty-three million dollar GPU cloud contract from an international AI model developer. Additionally, Russia's largest bank, Sber, has unveiled GigaChat 4, an AI model designed to solve complex tasks autonomously.

Switching to the weather in Rio de Janeiro. Today brings light showers with a high near eighty-two degrees Fahrenheit and a low around sixty-nine. There is a seventy-seven percent chance of rain, wind gusts up to thirty-six miles per hour, and a very high UV index of nine. Sunrise was at four fifty-eight a.m. and sunset will be at six twenty-two p.m. local time.

Finally, looking at news from Brazil and Rio. At least eight people died in Paraná and São Paulo after days of heavy rain caused severe storms and forced thousands from their homes, while food-supply agency Conab reports that Brazil's beef supply is set to tighten in two thousand twenty-seven. In Rio de Janeiro, the city government delivered forty-five new buses and created four new routes in the West Zone, and the state's exclusive prison for militia members is reportedly set to become a maximum-security facility. On the sports front, Palmeiras and Estudiantes de La Plata are set to play a single-match Libertadores final in Montevideo.

That's the paper.

title: Friday, November 27
script:
Good morning. Today is Friday, November twenty-seventh, twenty twenty-six.

Starting with the local forecast in Arkadelphia, expect sunny skies this afternoon with a high reaching sixty-one degrees before dropping to around fifty-six as the day winds down. Winds will remain light out of the west-southwest at under five miles per hour, with zero chance of rain. Tonight stays mostly clear as the temperature dips to thirty-seven degrees. Looking ahead to Saturday, expect mostly sunny conditions with a high near sixty-seven and wind gusts that could reach twenty miles per hour. The sun rose this morning at six fifty-six and will set at five oh three this evening.

Turning to the top headlines, millions of Americans spent Thanksgiving dealing with severe weather as a massive storm battered the East Coast. Nearly one million utility customers lost power due to high winds and heavy precipitation, and floodwaters swamped streets across the region. The severe conditions in New York prompted organizers to postpone the one-hundredth Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, leaving marching bands and travelers scrambling to adjust plans. Despite the weather and lingering worries over inflation, economists still expect holiday shoppers to spend at record levels as Black Friday sales get underway today, while the Dow closed out a holiday-shortened trading session to clinch its best week since twenty twenty-two.

Overseas, a French court has ordered veteran actor Gérard Depardieu to stand trial on charges of rape and sexual assault. The landmark ruling represents one of the highest-profile developments in France's reckoning with sexual misconduct across the arts, where the Me Too movement has often met stiff cultural resistance. In diplomacy, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized what he described as a strange relationship between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin during an interview with the BBC. Zelensky expressed frustration with Washington, arguing the United States is not putting enough pressure on Moscow to negotiate an end to the war as Kyiv braces for another harsh winter under bombardment. Meanwhile, Canada's Supreme Court has largely upheld a Quebec law that bans public servants, including teachers, from wearing religious symbols on the job, rejecting challenges from Muslim, Sikh, and Catholic groups.

In football, the Kansas City Chiefs suffered a painful Thanksgiving night loss in Buffalo, falling thirteen to ten to the Bills in freezing rain. Buffalo kicker Tyler Bass drilled a fifty-seven-yard field goal with just four seconds left on the clock to seal the win after a fifteen-yard punt return set the Bills up in Kansas City territory. The Chiefs had taken a ten to seven lead early in the third quarter on a one-yard touchdown plunge from Emmett Johnson, but the offense stalled down the stretch. Head coach Andy Reid questioned a controversial fourth-quarter replay review that overturned what had initially been ruled a third-down catch by Rashee Rice, saying the evidence to overturn it was not clear and obvious. The Chiefs also missed an opportunity with six minutes remaining when Harrison Butker pushed a forty-six-yard field goal wide right. On the injury front, wide receiver Jalen Royals was quickly ruled out in the second half with an ankle injury, and right guard Trey Smith was evaluated in the locker room late in the fourth quarter. The loss drops Kansas City a game behind the Denver Broncos in the American Football Conference West. Around the league, the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off an improbable comeback against Dallas on Thanksgiving, erasing a twenty-one-point deficit behind two long touchdown passes from quarterback Joe Milton to stun the Cowboys.

Over in college hoops, the Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team returns to Allen Fieldhouse this afternoon to host the Villanova Wildcats. Kansas is looking to build momentum on its home floor after a grueling road swing to Las Vegas and a recent tuneup against Denver. Tipoff in Lawrence is set for later today, giving the Jayhawks a high-profile holiday test against a traditional non-conference rival.

For fantasy managers setting lineups and planning ahead, injuries from the holiday slate are already complicating Week twelve plans. San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy missed another practice with an ankle injury, clouding his availability, while Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert remains in the league concussion protocol. In Jacksonville, wide receiver Parker Washington has been ruled out with a shoulder injury, opening the door for depth targets on the Jaguars roster. Chicago Bears rookie tight end Colston Loveland went down with an injury during Thursday's action, and Philadelphia wideout DeVonta Smith was seen limping after the Eagles' win, leaving his upcoming status uncertain. In Pittsburgh, veteran Mason Rudolph takes over under center after the Steelers decided to bench Aaron Rodgers, which could drastically alter the target distribution for Pittsburgh pass catchers. Managers should also monitor Arkansas running back Raheim Sanders, who is listed as questionable heading into the weekend.

Out west in Los Angeles, skies will be partly sunny today with very warm conditions, reaching an afternoon high near eighty-three degrees. Winds will be calm from the west-southwest at under five miles per hour, with no rain in sight. Tonight will bring increasing clouds and a low of fifty-nine degrees. Saturday should remain mostly cloudy, with afternoon highs cooling down slightly to around seventy-six degrees. The Los Angeles sunrise was at six thirty-seven this morning, and sunset comes early at four forty-three p.m.

In entertainment news, director Denis Villeneuve told Time Magazine that he is deeply disappointed with Disney's decision to schedule Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday on the very same December eighteenth weekend as his upcoming Dune: Part Three. Villeneuve pointed out that his previous two installments had to navigate pandemic disruptions, and this new scheduling clash creates a massive box office showdown. Speaking of ticket sales, Lionsgate's The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping had a huge Thanksgiving frame, pulling in eleven point six million dollars on Thursday. That marks the second-best Thanksgiving performance in franchise history, pushing the prequel's domestic cume to one hundred seventy-four point nine million dollars. Across the industry, unionization efforts hit a roadblock at Grand Theft Auto developer Rockstar Games, where over seventy-five percent of eligible staff voted against union recognition with the Independent Workers of Great Britain. Meanwhile, Toronto-based Wildling Pictures has secured screen rights to adapt two literary projects: Emily McBride's folk horror novel Queen Mab and Jason Bell's World War Two intelligence history, Operation Sparrow.

Turning to artificial intelligence and technology, Nvidia has instructed its manufacturing partners to temporarily pause shipments of advanced artificial intelligence servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. The hold comes as United States regulators tighten export curbs to prevent advanced semiconductor technology from being diverted into China through third-party hubs. Meanwhile, according to Chinese tech outlet thirty-six Kr, Elon Musk told staff that his company is trailing behind competitors in the AI model race, warning employees that anyone caught wasting graphics processing unit resources would be terminated. On the mobile front, Google is rolling out early testing for what it calls vibe-coded custom widgets on Android, allowing users to build personalized home screen tools. In India, BharatGen launched Patram one point five, a specialized enterprise model designed to streamline large-scale document processing and cut operational computing costs.

Heading south to Rio de Janeiro, conditions today are wet and cool. Expect steady drizzle throughout the day with a high near seventy-eight degrees and a low dipping to seventy. Rain chances sit at one hundred percent, accompanied by wind gusts reaching up to thirty-four miles per hour. Sunrise was at four fifty-eight in the morning local time, and the sun will set at six twenty-one this evening.

In Brazilian news, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva made a major shift toward the political center by appointing veteran Bradesco chairman Trabuco as the country's new finance minister. Financial markets responded with immediate enthusiasm: bank stocks surged on both local exchanges and Wall Street, and the Brazilian real gained three point six percent against the dollar. Speaking in Niterói, Lula sought to calm his political base by assuring voters that core welfare payments and educational funding would not be cut under the new leadership, even as the government tightens eligibility rules. On the trade front, Brazilian officials strongly rejected comments from French President Emmanuel Macron, who recently described Brazilian meat exports as doped while defending European Union restrictions before French agricultural groups. Locally in Rio de Janeiro, state health authorities have reinstated public reporting dashboards for Covid-nineteen tracking after a documented surge in infections that researchers believe may be tied to a newly circulating variant. In legal news, Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has officially granted permission for Mauro Cid to serve out his sentence locally in Rio.

That's the paper.

script:
Good morning. Today is Thursday, November 26, 2026. Let's get into the news.

Starting in Arkadelphia, today brings sunny skies with a high near fifty degrees. Northwest winds will blow at ten to fifteen miles per hour, with gusts reaching up to twenty-five miles per hour, and there is zero percent chance of rain. Major world headlines lead with escalating health crises, geopolitical tensions, and severe weather disruptions. On the fantasy football front, managers looking for waiver wire help and lineup advice ahead of week twelve can target emerging options like running back Chase Brown and wide receiver Rashee Rice, while keeping a close eye on extensive injury reports and player return timelines for stars like A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs.

Down in Rio de Janeiro, today brings heavy thunderstorms with a high near seventy-seven degrees Fahrenheit and a low around seventy-three. Expect a one-hundred-percent chance of rain, wind gusts reaching up to forty-four miles per hour, and a low UV index of one. Sunrise was at four-fifty-eight a.m., and sunset will be at six-twenty-one p.m., local time.

script:
Good morning. It is Wednesday, November twenty-fifth, twenty twenty-six.

In Hollywood and screenwriting news. Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday is making massive waves at the box office, hitting tracking firms with a record-breaking two hundred seventy million dollar initial forecast and more than one hundred million dollars already locked up in U.S. presales ahead of its December eighteenth release, alongside a newly announced Monopoly Go tie-in season. On the television side, HBO Max announced that its critically acclaimed medical drama The Pitt will premiere its third season on January seventh, twenty twenty-seven. Meanwhile, chef Gordon Ramsay is officially shifting from the kitchen to the race track, signing on to host the BBC's revived Top Gear four years after Andrew Flintoff's crash. In other project developments, Lily James is attached to star in and produce a feature adaptation of Lucy Foley's bestselling novel The Hunting Party for Universal Pictures, with Molly Sims also joining as a producer.

In retail tech, Amazon and Meta are reportedly in talks to lift a block on Meta's AI shopping agent, Muse, which would allow shoppers to browse and buy Black Friday deals directly through the chatbot while resolving ecommerce and advertising revenue concerns. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back against industry criticism, calling accusations that his company is surrendering human agency to artificial intelligence completely absurd. Checking the weather in Rio de Janeiro. Today brings severe thunderstorms with a hundred percent chance of rain, a high near ninety degrees, and a low around seventy-seven, with wind gusts reaching up to twenty-three miles per hour and a high UV index of eight. title: Monday, November 23
script:
Good morning, today is Monday, November twenty-third, twenty twenty-six.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, expect sunny skies this afternoon with a high near fifty-seven degrees, dropping into the low fifties later today under light north-northeast winds. Tonight turns partly cloudy as temperatures dip to a low around twenty-nine degrees. Looking ahead to Tuesday, it will be partly sunny with a high near fifty-one degrees and wind gusts reaching up to twenty miles per hour. Sunrise was at six fifty-two a.m. and sunset is at five oh four p.m., with zero percent chance of rain throughout the forecast.

Turning to top national and international headlines, Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive officer following his recent resignation over an extramarital affair. According to NPR and Yahoo Finance, the board voted unanimously to bring Huang back after finding no national security concerns, a move endorsed by President Trump that sent Nvidia stock soaring over thirty-one percent.

Overseas, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that naval drones successfully attacked and sank a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya. Per BBC News, the Kremlin warned of escalating regional tensions following the surprise strike far from the primary conflict zone.

In Washington, Democrats have officially achieved their largest House victory margin in fifty years, currently flipping forty-seven seats with the potential to reach forty-nine total. Meanwhile, the U.N. climate summit COP31 concluded in Turkey without reaching a final agreement, becoming the longest conference in the summit's history after running two days over schedule.

Finally, per NBC News, NATO is deploying early-warning aircraft to Poland after Russian missiles landed inside the country's borders, prompting immediate defense support for the alliance member.

Moving over to football, the Kansas City Chiefs picked up a dominant thirty-four to seven victory over the Arizona Cardinals in Week eleven. According to Arrowhead Pride, Patrick Mahomes delivered another stellar performance while defensive end George Karlaftis led the defense with two and a half sacks and a forced fumble. The win puts Kansas City at eight and two on the season, though the Denver Broncos currently hold the tiebreaker lead in the A-F-C West. To help boost their passing attack, Yahoo Sports reports the Chiefs traded for wide receiver Josh Downs ahead of their upcoming schedule.

Kansas City now turns its attention to a short week as they prepare to visit the nine-and-one Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night. Defensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy noted that the offense faces a steep test against Bills edge rusher Gregory Rousseau, who ranks second in the league with ten sacks. The Bills open as slight favorites for Thursday's game.

Elsewhere around the league, the Arizona Cardinals fired defensive coordinator Nick Rallis immediately following their blowout loss to Kansas City.

Shifting to college hoops, the Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team drops in the latest A-P Top Twenty-Five poll following their first loss of the season to Houston. According to Fox Four K-C, the Jayhawks were unable to hold off Houston, allowing the Cougars to jump seven spots to number one in the nation after a breakout performance by Mercy Miller.

Kansas returns to the court tonight in Lawrence to face the Denver Pioneers at eight p.m. Eastern time. Per SportsLine, the Jayhawks will look for a quick rebound on their home floor as they aim to reset their momentum early in the non-conference slate.

Looking at fantasy football for Week twelve, several key injuries are opening up opportunity across backfields. According to Yahoo Sports, Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan will miss time due to an injury, giving Jonathan Taylor an even larger share of touches. Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten is also dealing with an ankle stinger that puts his status in doubt for Sunday, making backup options a priority on the wire.

On the waiver wire, Washington running back Chris Rodriguez Junior and Baltimore back Justice Hill stand out as top targets for managers needing running back depth. For those searching for upside, Green Bay running back MarShawn Lloyd and wide receiver Ted Hurst the third are both featured as must-add pickups entering the week.

Out in Southern California, Los Angeles will see mostly sunny skies this afternoon with a comfortable high near sixty-nine degrees and a light west-southwest wind. Tonight brings mostly cloudy conditions as temperatures drop to around fifty-four degrees. Tuesday will be partly sunny with temperatures climbing to around seventy-three degrees. Sunrise was at six thirty-three a.m. and sunset will be at four forty-five p.m., with no rain in the forecast.

In entertainment news, Lionsgate has won a competitive spec script auction for the relationship dramedy Tell Me Everything. Per Variety, Dakota Johnson is attached to star and produce the project, which was written by Gaelyn Golde and follows a celebrity couples therapist dealing with her own marital breakdowns.

Over on television, Apple T-V has officially renewed Ted Lasso for a fifth season. Deadline reports that production is scheduled to begin on April fourteenth, with Jason Sudeikis returning to lead the hit comedy series.

Saturday Night Live has also announced its final hosts to close out the year. Timothée Chalamet and Robert De Niro will each host for their fourth time in December, with De Niro taking the stage on December twelfth and Chalamet hosting the Christmas episode on December nineteenth.

Finally, Amazon M-G-M Studios has expanded the cast of Christopher McQuarrie's upcoming untitled thriller. Vanessa Ferlito, John Carroll Lynch, and Ted Levine have joined the cast alongside Denzel Washington in the film scripted by Scott Barkan and Gregg Zehentner.

In technology, Anthropic has expanded its developer tools by launching Claude Ship, a new suite of features designed to automate software engineering. Per The Verge, the new beta features include automated agents that can review pull requests, resolve merge conflicts, and fix failing continuous integration checks directly within coding workflows.

Meanwhile, Amazon has acquired artificial intelligence startup Decart's optimization technology and research team in a seven point five billion dollar deal. Per TechCrunch, the purchase will support Amazon's infrastructure as it prepares to sell its custom Trainium chips to enterprise customers.

Google is also updating its Search A-I Mode by integrating personal data from Google Drive and Google Wallet to deliver customized responses.

On the legal front, Oregon and Virginia have filed state lawsuits against SpaceX and x-A-I over its chatbot Grok. The attorneys general allege the companies failed to implement basic safeguards to prevent the tool from generating sexualized deepfake images.

Down in Rio de Janeiro, expect light drizzle today with a high near ninety degrees Fahrenheit and a low of seventy-six tonight. There is a seventy-six percent chance of rain with wind gusts reaching up to twenty miles per hour and a high U-V index of nine. Sunrise was at four fifty-nine a.m. and sunset will be at six nineteen p.m. local time.

Turning to Brazil, economic officials have revised the nation's financial outlook for next year. Per MercoPress, the government lowered its twenty twenty-seven economic growth forecast to one point eight percent while raising inflation expectations toward the top of its target band. In political news, Brazil's Supreme Court issued a public summons for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro regarding alleged slander against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

Severe weather has also hit southern Brazil, where supercell storms in Rio Grande do Sul left five people dead and displaced more than twenty-five thousand residents.

In local news from Rio de Janeiro, CNN Brasil reports that City Hall has executed a new spending reduction plan targeting commissioned positions and job performance bonuses. Additionally, the Municipal Transport Company of Rio de Janeiro has opened a public hiring selection to recruit new articulated bus drivers across the city's transit system.

That's the paper.

title: Sunday, November 22
script:
Good morning. Today is Sunday, November 22, 2026.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, you can expect a high near seventy-three degrees today, though temperatures will drop to around sixty-seven degrees by the afternoon. Rain showers are likely before noon, followed by a chance of showers and thunderstorms between noon and two p.m., and a slight chance of lingering rain later in the day. Overall, skies will be mostly sunny with west-northwest winds around five to ten miles per hour and gusts as high as twenty miles per hour. The chance of precipitation today is fifty percent, with new rainfall amounts of less than a tenth of an inch expected. Tonight will bring partly cloudy skies with a low around thirty-nine degrees, accompanied by north-northeast winds from five to ten miles per hour and gusts up to twenty miles per hour. The chance of rain tonight drops to nine percent. Looking ahead to Monday, expect clear sunny skies with a high near fifty-seven degrees and northeast winds around five to ten miles per hour, gusting up to twenty miles per hour. Sunrise is at six fifty-one a.m. and sunset is at five zero four p.m. There are currently no active weather alerts for the area.

Turning now to the morning's top stories.

International climate negotiations at the COP thirty-one summit in Antalya, Turkey, have collapsed in their final hours after representatives from nearly two hundred countries failed to reach an agreement over fossil fuels. The annual talks ended in a deadlock over how to address the primary driver of global warming.

Travelers are facing major delays today after the Federal Aviation Administration reported that all Delta Air Lines flights have been grounded or delayed due to a widespread failure in an automated system. The disruption arrives right as millions of people begin traveling ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday week.

In legal developments, pharmaceutical giant Bayer has reached a settlement expected to cost the company billions of dollars to resolve thousands of claims involving non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The money will go toward individuals diagnosed with the blood cancer, which has been linked to the company's herbicide Roundup.

Over in international affairs, Finnish defense forces reported that a Russia-bound ship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday and had to be towed away. Finnish officials stated Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike, though authorities in Kyiv have not yet commented on the incident. Meanwhile, Mexican law enforcement officers arrested top drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as Chapo Isidro, following a intense shootout. Meza Flores was listed on the FBI's ten most wanted list on charges of drug trafficking and torture.

Moving over to sports and NFL action.

The Kansas City Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals at Arrowhead Stadium today in a noon kickoff broadcast on CBS. Kansas City comes into the matchup with a seven and two record, seeking a third straight victory to improve to eight and two ahead of their Thanksgiving night game against the Buffalo Bills. The Cardinals enter the contest at three and seven. Kansas City will be without running back Kenneth Walker, who is officially sidelined with an injury, while defensive tackle Peter Woods will miss his third consecutive game. To assist with roster depth, the Chiefs elevated running back Nate Carter and center Pete Nygra from the practice squad for today's matchup. For Arizona, veteran quarterback Josh Johnson will take the field to make the start, as rookie Carson Beck has been ruled out with back spasms.

Turning to Kansas Jayhawks basketball.

The Jayhawks are currently reviewing player evaluations and rotation grades following their early-season appearance in the Players Era Tournament, but there are no fresh game results or scheduled matchups on the court today for the Kansas men's basketball team.

Checking in on fantasy football.

Injury updates are reshaping starting lineups as fantasy managers finalize their Week eleven rosters before kickoff. Kansas City running back Kenneth Walker has been officially ruled out once again, leaving managers to search for replacement options. On the positive side, running back Kyle Monangai is set to return to action today after clearing his injury report.

At tight end, Buffalo's Dalton Kincaid has fantasy owners monitoring his status closely following late-week health updates, while Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers remains uncertain for today's matchup against Denver. Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey is another key player to check before game time against the Jets. For managers looking to bolster their roster through the waiver wire, quarterback Cam Ward is drawing heavy interest as a top pickup target for the upcoming week.

Now for a look at your Los Angeles weather.

Los Angeles will see partly sunny skies today with a high near sixty-eight degrees and light west-southwest winds around five miles per hour. Rain showers are likely to develop after four p.m., with a sixty percent chance of precipitation and new rainfall amounts under a tenth of an inch expected. Tonight, rain showers remain likely before four a.m. under partly cloudy skies, with a low around fifty-three degrees and north-northwest winds around five miles per hour. The chance of rain tonight remains at sixty percent, with light accumulation under a tenth of an inch. Monday brings a return to full sun with a high near sixty-nine degrees and north-northeast winds around five miles per hour. Sunrise is at six thirty-two a.m. and sunset is at four forty-five p.m. There are no active weather alerts in effect.

Shifting over to entertainment news.

The Hunger Games franchise made a massive return to the global box office over the weekend. Lionsgate's dystopian prequel, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, posted a sensational domestic opening debut of one hundred twenty million dollars. Internationally, the film added one hundred five million dollars across eighty-four overseas territories, bringing its worldwide premiere total to two hundred twenty-five million dollars.

In film news, Oscar-nominated director Luca Guadagnino confirmed that his proposed adaptation of American Psycho with screenwriter Scott Z. Burns is no longer moving forward. Guadagnino announced during a podcast appearance that he has stepped away from the Lionsgate project after two years of development.

Filmmaker Robert Eggers revealed he plans to take a break from the horror genre following the release of his upcoming feature Werwulf. Eggers stated that after spending more than a decade directing folklore horror projects, he is ready to explore different genres for his next film.

In labor developments, Screen Actors Guild President Sean Astin announced the formation of the President's Healthcare Task Force. The initiative is aimed at addressing systemic issues in union healthcare access, as a substantial majority of SAG-AFTRA members currently fail to meet the earnings threshold required to qualify for union health insurance.

Finally, former Denver Broncos All-Pro linebacker and longtime ESPN broadcaster Tom Jackson has passed away at the age of seventy-five. Jackson spent nearly thirty years with ESPN as a leading studio analyst, working alongside Chris Berman on Sunday NFL Countdown and SportsCenter.

Moving into technology and artificial intelligence.

Encrypted messaging platform Signal is rolling out new restrictions that limit mobile screenshots within its iOS and Android applications. Company officials stated the decision was made to protect user privacy against the growing threat of AI-powered automated surveillance and data extraction.

At the United Nations in Geneva, international delegates concluded a week of high-level talks without reaching an agreement on legally binding rules for autonomous weapons systems, commonly known as killer robots. Representatives agreed only to continue discussing future policy options, failing to meet calls from the International Committee of the Red Cross for immediate regulations within the year.

In the gaming world, the developer behind The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus removed several music tracks from the game following widespread player backlash on Steam. Creator Edmund McMillen apologized to fans after users discovered that audio files in a Grand Theft Auto parody section contained Suno metadata indicating the use of generative AI music, stating he was unaware the tracks had been generated by artificial intelligence.

Checking the weather in Rio de Janeiro.

Rio de Janeiro will experience overcast conditions today with a high near eighty-nine degrees Fahrenheit and a low around seventy-eight degrees. There is a forty-five percent chance of rain throughout the day, with wind gusts reaching up to twenty-eight miles per hour and a high UV index of nine. Sunrise was at four fifty-nine a.m. local time, and sunset will be at six eighteen p.m.

Ending today with news from Brazil.

Severe weather has struck southern Brazil, where a violent storm system in Rio Grande do Sul has raised the death toll to five people, with more than two hundred fifty others injured amid widespread damage across the region.

In Rio de Janeiro, thousands of attendees gathered along the Copacabana beachfront for the annual LGBTI+ Pride Parade, turning the main avenue into a major celebration of civil rights and community resistance.

During a live concert performance in Rio, international pop star Mariah Carey addressed recent media rumors concerning her health directly from the stage, telling the crowd not to make her angry before continuing her set.

In local crime news, Rio authorities have opened an investigation into the fatal shooting of a thirty-eight-year-old public figure who was killed during a visit to the city.

That's the paper.
